tool_schemas.name: pdf_url
tool_schemas.description: Searches Korean law resources for the provided query string and returns a list of discovered PDF URLs associated with a stored search request. Results may be returned incrementally as new URLs are discovered for the same query; if multiple URLs are available, the response contains the full current set for that request (no pagination parameters are supported). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if query is missing/blank, UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN if the caller is not permitted to search, QUOTA_EXCEEDED if search limits are exceeded, and UPSTREAM_ERROR if the remote resource cannot be queried.
tool_schemas.implementation:
def pdf_url(query, **_extra):
    import json, os, datetime, hashlib, re, time, urllib.parse

    _DB = __import__("os").environ.get("MCP_DB_DIR") or ("./environment_mix/0499000" if __import__("os").path.isdir("./environment_mix/0499000") else "/app/database")
    def _load(n):
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f)
        except Exception: return []
    def _save(n, d):
        with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(d, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    def _err(code, msg, **x): return {"error": {"code": code, "message": msg, **x}}

    t0 = time.time()
    now = datetime.datetime.utcnow().replace(microsecond=0).isoformat() + "Z"

    # No explicit request log/usage collections exist in schema; nothing to record/enforce.

    # Validate
    if not isinstance(query, str):
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "query must be a string")
    raw_query = query
    if len(raw_query) < 1 or len(raw_query) > 512:
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "query length must be between 1 and 512")

    def _normalize_query(s: str) -> str:
        s = s.strip()
        s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
        # canonicalize common punctuation variants
        s = s.replace("“", '"').replace("”", '"').replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'")
        s = s.replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")
        s = re.sub(r"\s*([,;:(){}\[\]])\s*", r"\1", s)
        return s

    def _hash_text(s: str) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    def _canonicalize_url(u: str) -> str:
        u = (u or "").strip()
        try:
            p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(u)
        except Exception:
            return u
        scheme = (p.scheme or "").lower()
        netloc = (p.netloc or "").strip()
        path = p.path or ""
        query_s = p.query or ""
        frag = ""  # drop fragment
        # normalize host case; keep userinfo/port if present (rare)
        if "@" in netloc:
            ui, hostport = netloc.rsplit("@", 1)
            hostport = hostport.lower()
            netloc = ui + "@" + hostport
        else:
            netloc = netloc.lower()
        # collapse multiple slashes
        path = re.sub(r"/{2,}", "/", path)
        # percent-encode minimally (avoid raising)
        try:
            path = urllib.parse.quote(urllib.parse.unquote(path), safe="/:@-._~%!$&'()*+,;=")
        except Exception:
            pass
        # sort query params for stable hashing
        if query_s:
            try:
                q = urllib.parse.parse_qsl(query_s, keep_blank_values=True)
                q.sort()
                query_s = urllib.parse.urlencode(q, doseq=True)
            except Exception:
                pass
        return urllib.parse.urlunsplit((scheme, netloc, path, query_s, frag))

    search_queries = _load("search_queries.json")
    pdf_candidates = _load("pdf_candidates.json")

    normalized = _normalize_query(raw_query)
    qhash = _hash_text(normalized)

    # Upsert search_queries by unique(query_hash)
    sq = None
    for row in search_queries:
        if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("query_hash") == qhash:
            sq = row
            break

    if sq is None:
        sq_id = "sq_" + hashlib.sha256((qhash + "|" + now).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:24]
        sq = {
            "id": sq_id,
            "query_text": raw_query,
            "query_hash": qhash,
            "normalized_query_text": normalized,
            "status": "received",
            "result_count": 0,
            "error_message": None,
            "created_at": now,
            "updated_at": now,
        }
        search_queries.append(sq)
    else:
        # keep original query_text but refresh updated fields for observability
        sq["query_text"] = sq.get("query_text") or raw_query
        sq["normalized_query_text"] = normalized
        sq["updated_at"] = now

    # Transition received->searching (or remain searching) for this invocation
    status = sq.get("status")
    if status in ("completed", "failed"):
        # return current set (no new discovery without external search in this offline implementation)
        sq_id = sq["id"]
        candidates = [c for c in pdf_candidates if c.get("search_query_id") == sq_id]
        candidates.sort(key=lambda x: (x.get("rank") or 10**9, x.get("created_at") or ""))
        # Ensure ranks consecutive if present; if data is inconsistent, do not mutate silently
        urls = [c.get("url") for c in candidates if isinstance(c.get("url"), str)]
        return {
            "search_query": sq,
            "urls": urls,
            "pdf_candidates": candidates,
        }

    transitions = {
        "received": {"searching", "failed"},
        "searching": {"completed", "failed"},
        "completed": set(),
        "failed": set(),
    }
    if status is None:
        sq["status"] = "received"
        status = "received"
    if "searching" not in transitions.get(status, set()) and status != "searching":
        return _err("INVALID_TRANSITION", f"Cannot transition search_queries.status from {status} to searching")

    if status != "searching":
        sq["status"] = "searching"
        sq["updated_at"] = now

    # Offline discovery strategy:
    # If query itself is a URL, treat as the single candidate; otherwise, no external search.
    discovered_urls = []
    q_stripped = raw_query.strip()
    if re.match(r"^https?://", q_stripped, re.IGNORECASE):
        discovered_urls = [q_stripped]

    # Populate candidates enforcing unique(search_query_id, url_hash) and consecutive ranks
    sq_id = sq["id"]
    existing = [c for c in pdf_candidates if c.get("search_query_id") == sq_id]
    existing_by_hash = {}
    max_rank = 0
    for c in existing:
        uh = c.get("url_hash")
        if isinstance(uh, str):
            existing_by_hash[uh] = c
        r = c.get("rank")
        if isinstance(r, int) and r > max_rank:
            max_rank = r

    created_any = False
    for u in discovered_urls:
        cu = _canonicalize_url(u)
        uh = _hash_text(cu)
        if uh in existing_by_hash:
            # idempotent: refresh url field/canonical changes not stored; just touch updated_at
            existing_by_hash[uh]["updated_at"] = now
            continue
        max_rank += 1
        cand_id = "pc_" + hashlib.sha256((sq_id + "|" + uh + "|" + str(max_rank)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:24]
        try:
            host = urllib.parse.urlsplit(cu).netloc or None
        except Exception:
            host = None
        pdf_candidates.append({
            "id": cand_id,
            "search_query_id": sq_id,
            "url": cu,
            "url_hash": uh,
            "source_host": host,
            "title": None,
            "rank": max_rank,
            "status": "discovered",
            "http_status_last": None,
            "content_type_last": None,
            "content_length_last_bytes": None,
            "created_at": now,
            "updated_at": now,
        })
        created_any = True

    # Ensure ranks are consecutive starting at 1 for this query (only validate among current records)
    candidates_now = [c for c in pdf_candidates if c.get("search_query_id") == sq_id]
    ranks = sorted([c.get("rank") for c in candidates_now if isinstance(c.get("rank"), int)])
    if ranks:
        expected = list(range(1, len(ranks) + 1))
        if ranks != expected:
            # Refuse to claim completed if invariant broken; do not "fix" silently.
            sq["status"] = "failed" if "failed" in transitions.get("searching", set()) else sq.get("status")
            sq["error_message"] = "Candidate ranks are not consecutive starting at 1"
            sq["updated_at"] = now
            _save("search_queries.json", search_queries)
            _save("pdf_candidates.json", pdf_candidates)
            return _err("CONFLICT", "Candidate ranks invariant violated for search_query", search_query_id=sq_id)

    # Complete lifecycle searching->completed (or failed)
    if "completed" not in transitions.get("searching", set()):
        return _err("INVALID_TRANSITION", "Cannot transition search_queries.status to completed")

    sq["result_count"] = len(candidates_now)
    sq["error_message"] = None

    sq["status"] = "completed"
    sq["updated_at"] = now

    _save("search_queries.json", search_queries)
    if created_any:
        _save("pdf_candidates.json", pdf_candidates)
    else:
        # still save candidates if we touched updated_at on existing ones
        _save("pdf_candidates.json", pdf_candidates)

    candidates_now.sort(key=lambda x: (x.get("rank") or 10**9, x.get("created_at") or ""))
    urls = [c.get("url") for c in candidates_now if isinstance(c.get("url"), str)]

    _ = time.time() - t0
    return {
        "search_query": sq,
        "urls": urls,
        "pdf_candidates": candidates_now,
    }

tool_schemas.name: load_pdf
tool_schemas.description: Creates or reuses a PDF fetch/parse job for the provided query (a PDF URL or a known PDF identifier) and returns the job record and, when available, the extracted text content. If processing is not yet complete, the response indicates the current job state and can be called again to retrieve the completed content (no pagination parameters are supported). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if query is missing/blank or not a supported PDF reference, NOT_FOUND if the referenced PDF URL was not previously discovered/registered, CONFLICT if the PDF is in a state that cannot transition to processing (e.g., already processing or permanently failed), UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN if the caller is not permitted to load/process PDFs, and QUOTA_EXCEEDED if processing limits are exceeded.
tool_schemas.implementation:
def load_pdf(query, **_extra):
    import json, os, datetime, hashlib, re, time, urllib.parse

    _DB = __import__("os").environ.get("MCP_DB_DIR") or ("./environment_mix/0499000" if __import__("os").path.isdir("./environment_mix/0499000") else "/app/database")
    def _load(n):
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f)
        except Exception: return []
    def _save(n, d):
        with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(d, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    def _err(code, msg, **x): return {"error": {"code": code, "message": msg, **x}}

    t0 = time.time()
    now = datetime.datetime.utcnow().replace(microsecond=0).isoformat() + "Z"

    if not isinstance(query, str):
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "query must be a string")
    if len(query) < 1 or len(query) > 2048:
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "query length must be between 1 and 2048")

    def _hash_text(s: str) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    def _canonicalize_url(u: str) -> str:
        u = (u or "").strip()
        try:
            p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(u)
        except Exception:
            return u
        scheme = (p.scheme or "").lower()
        netloc = (p.netloc or "").strip()
        path = p.path or ""
        query_s = p.query or ""
        frag = ""
        if "@" in netloc:
            ui, hostport = netloc.rsplit("@", 1)
            hostport = hostport.lower()
            netloc = ui + "@" + hostport
        else:
            netloc = netloc.lower()
        path = re.sub(r"/{2,}", "/", path)
        try:
            path = urllib.parse.quote(urllib.parse.unquote(path), safe="/:@-._~%!$&'()*+,;=")
        except Exception:
            pass
        if query_s:
            try:
                q = urllib.parse.parse_qsl(query_s, keep_blank_values=True)
                q.sort()
                query_s = urllib.parse.urlencode(q, doseq=True)
            except Exception:
                pass
        return urllib.parse.urlunsplit((scheme, netloc, path, query_s, frag))

    search_queries = _load("search_queries.json")
    pdf_candidates = _load("pdf_candidates.json")
    pdf_documents = _load("pdf_documents.json")
    pdf_load_jobs = _load("pdf_load_jobs.json")
    pdf_extractions = _load("pdf_extractions.json")

    # Create load job (must exist even if resolution fails)
    job_id = "lj_" + hashlib.sha256((query + "|" + now).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:24]
    job = {
        "id": job_id,
        "input_query_text": query,
        "search_query_id": None,
        "pdf_candidate_id": None,
        "pdf_document_id": None,
        "resolved_url": None,
        "status": "queued",
        "failure_stage": None,
        "error_message": None,
        "started_at": None,
        "finished_at": None,
        "created_at": now,
        "updated_at": now,
    }
    pdf_load_jobs.append(job)

    def _set_job_failed(stage: str, msg: str):
        # queued->failed is allowed; fetching/parsing too, but we only transition forward here.
        job["status"] = "failed"
        job["failure_stage"] = stage
        job["error_message"] = msg
        job["finished_at"] = now
        job["updated_at"] = now

    # Resolve to URL
    resolved_url = None
    candidate_row = None

    q_strip = query.strip()
    if re.match(r"^https?://", q_strip, re.IGNORECASE):
        resolved_url = _canonicalize_url(q_strip)
        # Link to candidate if exists (exact or canonical match)
        canon = resolved_url
        canon_hash = _hash_text(canon)
        for c in pdf_candidates:
            u = c.get("url")
            if not isinstance(u, str):
                continue
            cu = _canonicalize_url(u)
            if u == q_strip or cu == canon or _hash_text(cu) == canon_hash:
                candidate_row = c
                break
    else:
        # Not a URL: try to match by exact candidate url equal to query
        for c in pdf_candidates:
            u = c.get("url")
            if isinstance(u, str) and u == q_strip:
                candidate_row = c
                resolved_url = _canonicalize_url(u)
                break

    if candidate_row is not None:
        job["pdf_candidate_id"] = candidate_row.get("id")
        job["search_query_id"] = candidate_row.get("search_query_id")

    if resolved_url is None:
        _set_job_failed("resolve", "Could not resolve query to a PDF URL")
        _save("pdf_load_jobs.json", pdf_load_jobs)
        return {
            "job": job,
            "pdf_document": None,
            "extraction": None,
            "text": None,
        }

    job["resolved_url"] = resolved_url

    # Upsert pdf_documents by canonical_url_hash
    curl = resolved_url
    curl_hash = _hash_text(curl)
    doc = None
    for d in pdf_documents:
        if isinstance(d, dict) and d.get("canonical_url_hash") == curl_hash:
            doc = d
            break
    if doc is None:
        doc_id = "pd_" + hashlib.sha256((curl_hash + "|" + now).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:24]
        doc = {
            "id": doc_id,
            "canonical_url": curl,
            "canonical_url_hash": curl_hash,
            "status": "new",
            "etag": None,
            "last_modified": None,
            "sha256_bytes": None,
            "byte_size": None,
            "stored_object_key": None,
            "last_fetch_at": None,
            "created_at": now,
            "updated_at": now,
        }
        pdf_documents.append(doc)
    else:
        doc["updated_at"] = now

    job["pdf_document_id"] = doc.get("id")

    # Simulated processing pipeline (offline):
    # If document already available and extraction ready exists, immediately complete.
    # Otherwise, move to failed at fetch stage (since we cannot actually fetch offline).
    def _find_extraction_for_doc(doc_id: str):
        for e in pdf_extractions:
            if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("pdf_document_id") == doc_id:
                return e
        return None

    extraction = _find_extraction_for_doc(doc["id"])

    # If there is an existing ready extraction, we can complete the job (parsing implied already done)
    if extraction is not None and extraction.get("status") == "ready":
        # queued -> fetching -> parsing -> completed (must respect transitions)
        job["status"] = "fetching"
        job["started_at"] = job["started_at"] or now
        job["updated_at"] = now

        job["status"] = "parsing"
        job["updated_at"] = now

        job["status"] = "completed"
        job["finished_at"] = now
        job["updated_at"] = now

        _save("pdf_documents.json", pdf_documents)
        _save("pdf_load_jobs.json", pdf_load_jobs)
        _save("pdf_extractions.json", pdf_extractions)

        text = extraction.get("text_content")
        return {
            "job": job,
            "pdf_document": doc,
            "extraction": extraction,
            "text": text,
        }

    # Otherwise, we cannot fetch/parse offline. Mark failed at fetch stage.
    # Also, reflect candidate status transition if linked and appropriate.
    if candidate_row is not None:
        # candidate: discovered->fetch_scheduled is allowed; fetch_failed->fetch_scheduled also allowed
        cstatus = candidate_row.get("status")
        cand_transitions = {
            "discovered": {"filtered", "fetch_scheduled"},
            "filtered": set(),
            "fetch_scheduled": {"fetched", "fetch_failed"},
            "fetched": set(),
            "fetch_failed": {"fetch_scheduled"},
        }
        if cstatus in cand_transitions and "fetch_scheduled" in cand_transitions[cstatus]:
            candidate_row["status"] = "fetch_scheduled"
            candidate_row["updated_at"] = now

    # Move job queued->fetching then fail fetch
    job["status"] = "fetching"
    job["started_at"] = job["started_at"] or now
    job["updated_at"] = now

    _set_job_failed("fetch", "Offline mode: fetching not available; cannot download PDF bytes")

    # Ensure failure_stage populated when failed (business rule already met)
    _save("pdf_candidates.json", pdf_candidates)
    _save("pdf_documents.json", pdf_documents)
    _save("pdf_load_jobs.json", pdf_load_jobs)

    _ = time.time() - t0
    return {
        "job": job,
        "pdf_document": doc,
        "extraction": extraction,
        "text": extraction.get("text_content") if extraction and extraction.get("status") == "ready" else None,
    }

tool_schemas.name: list_search_queries
tool_schemas.description: Lists stored search request records, optionally filtered by status or query_hash, returning the most recent first. Refuses invalid filters and enforces pagination limits.

status.description: Filter by search query lifecycle status.

created_after.description: Only return records created at or after this time (ISO 8601).

created_before.description: Only return records created before this time (ISO 8601).

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.

tool_schemas.name: get_search_query
tool_schemas.description: Fetches a single stored search request by id. Refuses unknown ids.

id.description: Primary key of the search_queries record.

tool_schemas.name: list_pdf_candidates
tool_schemas.description: Lists discovered PDF URL candidates for a search query, optionally filtered by status. Refuses invalid search_query_id and enforces pagination limits.

search_query_id.description: Parent search_queries id to list candidates for.

source_host.description: Filter by exact source host (e.g., domain).

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.

tool_schemas.name: get_pdf_document
tool_schemas.description: Fetches a single PDF document record by id, including its current fetch availability state. Refuses unknown ids.

id.description: Primary key of the pdf_documents record.

tool_schemas.name: get_pdf_load_job
tool_schemas.description: Fetches a single PDF load job by id. Returns current status and any linked document/extraction identifiers; refuses unknown ids.

id.description: Primary key of the pdf_load_jobs record.

metadata.name: Law Tool KOR
metadata.description: This backend supports searching Korean law resources for PDF documents and loading/processing those PDFs. It stores search requests, discovered PDF URLs, PDF fetch/parse jobs, and the extracted text content for downstream use. Repository: https://github.com/drepion43/law_tool_KOR Homepage: https://s
